promise: Repeal and replace Obamacare 'very quickly' in 2017
description: Trump repeatedly promised the Affordable Care Act would be repealed and replaced 'very quickly' after taking office. The Senate repeal effort collapsed on July 28, 2017 with John McCain's decisive vote, and the ACA remained law.

review.note: July 28 repeal defeat supported. January 20 attribution and December 31 deadline for 'very quickly' need contemporaneous promise source. Through-2026 legal assertion not checked.

promise: Musk forecast a fully autonomous Tesla demonstration from Los Angeles to New York by the end of 2017.
description: Musk forecast an autonomous coast-to-coast Tesla demonstration by the end of 2017. In February 2018 he acknowledged missing that target.
evidence: The dated TED interview establishes the original end-2017 target.
In Tesla's February 7, 2018 earnings call, Musk acknowledged the missed demonstration target. This assessment concerns that deadline, not all later autonomous-driving capability.
sources: Tesla earnings call via ROIC AI

promise: Produce 5,000 Model 3 cars per week by the end of 2017
description: Tesla reached a production rate of approximately 5,000 Model 3 vehicles per week in 2018, after its stated 2017 target.
evidence: Tesla's second-quarter 2018 report says approximately 5,000 Model 3s were produced in multiple July weeks.

review.note: Tesla filing supports achieving roughly 5,000/week in 2018, including multiple July weeks. May 3 2017 original forecast still needs original letter. 'Overnight shutdown push' unsupported; outcome was delayed achievement rather than partial production rate.

promise: Solar Roof tiles (unveiled Oct 28, 2016) to begin installations by summer 2017
description: Tesla reported initial Solar Roof installations on employee homes in August 2017. These preceded broader customer availability.

review.note: Employee installations already existed in August 2017. Whether pledge required general customers remains unresolved; original June date and December deadline conflict with stated unveiling/summer timing.

promise: The Bank of England projected UK GDP growth of 1.4% in 2017 in its November 2016 Inflation Report (forecast, not a promise).
description: The Bank's November 3, 2016 Inflation Report projected 1.4% UK GDP growth in 2017, rather than 0.4%. This was a forecast conditional on its economic assumptions.
evidence: Outcome not established as of 2026-09-21: no consistent ONS outturn vintage was established for comparison; the original growth and unemployment figures are removed.

promise: Bring France's public deficit below 3% of GDP in 2017
description: Le Maire reiterated the commitment to bring the 2017 deficit below 3% of GDP, conditional on spending restraint. INSEE's March 2018 first estimate reported a 2017 deficit of 2.6% of GDP.
evidence: TF1's dated interview records the 2017 commitment.
INSEE's first 2017 deficit estimate was below the 3% threshold.

promise: 2007 bet with Protégé Partners: over Jan 1, 2008 - Dec 31, 2017, an S&P 500 index fund would beat a fund-of-funds portfolio of hedge funds
description: Buffett won the ten-year wager ending in 2017. His 2017 shareholder letter reports a 125.8% cumulative gain and 8.5% annualized gain for the S&P index fund, exceeding each of the five competing funds of funds.
evidence: Buffett dates the wager to 19 December 2007 and publishes the final fund-by-fund scorecard.

promise: IBM would return to revenue growth in 2017
description: Rometty promised investors that IBM would return to revenue growth as its strategic imperatives scaled. IBM grew in the fourth quarter of 2017, but full-year 2017 revenue still declined slightly year over year (roughly $79.1 billion versus about $79.9 billion in 2016); sustained full-year growth resumed only in 2018.
evidence: Q4 2017 returned to growth, but FY2017 revenue was still down ~1%
IBM reported full-year revenue growth again in 2018

review.note: Full-year revenue was $79.1 billion, down about 1%, while Q4 revenue rose 3.6%. Those outcomes are established, but the alleged January 1 promise and whether it required annual growth or an exit-quarter return to growth are not. That distinction controls the verdict.
